note.p: See Ed Pope's note: In his will PCC 1800 John Warner made Philip Courtenay, then at Charterhouse School, his heir and left rings to Matthew Raine, Jonathan Raine, miss Raine, mrs Raine, Sir Richard Colt Hoare, Major Cartwright, John Horne Tooke, miss Hart and her sister Charlotte, Sir Francis Burdett, Robert Fergusson, Charles Warren, William Hayley, William Long, William Bosville, William Frend, Stephen Tucker, Hugh Bell, Henry Cline, Thomas Thompson, John Cleaver Banks, Charles Morgan, Thomas Wakefield and his brother Gilbert, and William Scott, to whom he also left, after Tooke's death, his tankard, in memory of his friendship with Scott's grandfather, father and mother (Wm Scott d 1767 master of Southampton grammar school, James Scott will PCC 1794, and Jane Elizabeth nee Harmood). This is a roll call of Tooke's Wimbledon set. Philip Courtenay was probably an illegitimate son of John Warner, who never married, or else his adopted son. He married Louisa dau of Hugh Bell in 1812. His will PCC 1842.
